summary:
Traced every tick-to-clock/date conversion. There are 9 independent implementations plus about a dozen data/copy layers where a human typed a clock time or duration beside a tick. Five different times are shown for tick 28 (Reynolds killed), and none of them matches the 10:15 AM in the monument text and vignette V-002.

**Why the map is off**
- Main-map clock: the store's getTickTime (bundle.pretty.js:9371-9383, line 9377) starts Day 1 at 06:00 and Days 2-3 at 04:00. The data declares 5:00am on every day.
- The hand-typed Day-1 chronology labels add a further +5 min from tick 12 on. That gives tick 17 as 7:20 on the map vs 6:25am in the data (+55 min), and tick 451 as 4:00 vs 5:00am (-60 min).
- The 06:00/04:00 constants are absent from the Jun-13 build. They came in with a later store-only patch.
- Date +2 (C3): a literal `+ 2` in the HUD badge (97428), the monument tooltip (100842) and the ancestor timeline (101006). It has been there since the Jun-13 build; only the store copy was ever fixed. The store also prints "July 1, 12:xx AM" for ticks 217-225.

**Findings not in the audit**
- Deep links: the deployed map reads only `?ancestor=` (101019). The share builder's `?t=`, nine link builders' `?tick=`/`?unit=`/`?vignette=`/`?lat=&lng=`, and the guide's "Share a permalink" are all dead.
- Seek bug: the forward-fill cache `i2` (96265) is never cleared, so backward seeks draw stale future positions.
- Sparse keyframes: placements are 1,804 keyframes for 478 units, populated on only 188 of 675 ticks. The schema promises 430,000+ records. Interpolation exists only between adjacent ticks.
- Event triggers are exact-tick and can be skipped at high speed.
- Desktop overlays (HUD, time bar, event cards) are mounted in the Mobile layout too.
- The bundle file `index-Cg8FAMXN.js` has been patched in place under the same hashed name. With `immutable` caching and a cache-first service worker, any time fix must ship under a new file name.

**Evidence**
- The site's own casualty data implies 1.5 to 5 min per tick; kinematics implies at least 5 min per tick on the Day-1 approach march; the July-2 morning runs about 24-32 min per tick. No single formula fits.
- Against 27 of the site's own authored times, today's clocks are off by a mean of about 4.6-4.9 h, always too early.
- The time-facts specialist's independent sourced CSVs give a mean of about 4.9 h over 134 events. Their 33-anchor proposal loads into my module unchanged, and the module's inverse matches their independent tick_under_proposed_anchors on 129 of 129 facts (worst difference 0.05 tick).
- About 74% of chronology events are pure relabels. 27 (19%) are content defects no clock can fix: 12 misordered, 4 wrong-day, 9 composite, 2 unverified quotes.

**Decision**
- Adopt (a): a piecewise-linear time-warp through verified anchors. Ticks stay permanent frame IDs, and clock time becomes a derived monotone function.
- Reject (b), a true 5-minute grid. It would need generating placements that do not exist, and it breaks all bookmarks and links. Constant-clock playback is delivered as a runtime mode instead.

**Deliverables**
- Full formula inventory with example outputs, root-cause proofs, and the anchor JSON schema plus fit algorithm.
- Consumer-by-consumer consequences, URL contract, and migration plan with rollout hazards.
- Validator spec (V1-V15) and tests.
- Exact patch locations for the bundle, the reconstructed source tree, 16 sub-pages, data files and copy.
- A tested reference module (13/13 tests pass) and 20 fix specs.

Everything in the report that depends on the specialist's CSVs is regenerated by `assemble.py`. I checked their anchor proposal for internal consistency only, not against 1863 sources.

findings.title: Phase-0 hotfix: one date and one clock that at least agree with each other
findings.evidence: bundle.pretty.js:97428 `July ${l + 2}, 1863`; :100842 (JF) `July ${f + 2}`; :101006 (QF) `July ${f + 2}`; store 9377 `(P === 1 ? 6 * 60 : 4 * 60)` vs M4 9859 / JF 100838 / QF 101001 `5 * 60`; event card prints hand-typed JSON label at 98630; store prints 'July 1, 12:xx AM' for ticks 217-225. Same tick 28 shows 8:15 AM, 7:20am, 7:15 AM July 3, July 3 7:15 AM, 'July 3, 1863'.
findings.root_cause: Four independent copies of one formatter; the +2 is original (present in the Jun-13 build), only the store copy was fixed; 06:00/04:00 was a later store-only patch; no test.
findings.fix: Six string edits applied to bundle.pretty.js and the minified bundle: store base to 5*60; HUD `July ${l}`; speed label `${f}x`; JF takes the day from the tick (drop monument.day) and no +2; QF no +2; event-card header uses the same formula as the toolbar. Ship under a NEW content-hashed file name (index.html, sw.js PRECACHE_ASSETS and CACHE_NAME updated together).
findings.acceptance_test: For ticks {1,12,17,28,226,451,538,675} every DOM date string shows July 1-3 and every clock string is identical across toolbar, mobile header, time bar, HUD, monument tooltip, ancestor row and event card; grep for date templates with +N returns 0.
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: C3 closed; C4 'clock disagrees with itself' closed; Historical/data consistency C- toward B (history itself still off until 02-05)
findings.correction: Evidence exact (9377, 9859, 97428-97429, 100838/100842, 101001/101006, 98630; Jun-13 build has k=5*60+H and July ${R+2}; strings exist and are unique in the minified bundle). Corrections: (1) renaming the entry chunk is not enough. HelpModal-CFV9T0zH.js and BookmarkPanel-C5YT4b5k.js both begin import{...}from"./index-Cg8FAMXN.js" and are served immutable (local files and live curl). Rewrite their bytes (new names) and update the import() strings at 112469-112470, otherwise Help/Bookmarks load a second copy of the old entry (duplicate React/zustand). (2) Section 9 says Phase 0 removes the contradictory tooltips. That is false: mon_hood (tick 262) would print '8:00 AM July 2' above typed text 'wounded ... at 4:00 PM July 2'; only the date is repaired. (3) Phase 0 leaves the toolbar printing the date twice (113084-113088).

findings.title: Canonical time module + time_anchors.json (piecewise-linear time-warp; ticks stay permanent frame IDs)
findings.evidence: 9 independent tick-to-clock implementations (store 9371-9383; HUD 97428; JF 100836; QF 100998; M4/E4 9856-9884; compare.html:120-129; living-ledger.html:135-144; camera.html:175-179; immersive.html:169-173). Data proves a variable-rate time-lapse: casualty file 1.5 min/tick (charge, ticks 538-558), 1.6 (July-2 afternoon), 5.1 (Culp's Hill), Day-1 approach march needs >= 5 min/tick, July-2 morning ~24-32 min/tick. Only 188 of 675 ticks carry placements, so a true 5-minute grid (option b) cannot exist without inventing data.
findings.root_cause: No shared time abstraction; each surface re-implemented a 5-min formula with different constants; the data was authored as a compressed narrative, not on a uniform clock.
findings.fix: Add tickToClock/clockToTick/format/tabDay/minutesPerTick/tickAfterMinutes over a strictly-monotone anchor table (module tested in tmp-app-time/time-model.mjs, ~75 lines, zero deps); local mean time, date rolls over at midnight independent of the Day tab, no extrapolation, append-only ticks, uncertainty (sigma) per anchor, gaps[] policy, UI rounding to 5 min. Generate /data/ticks.json (675 rows) and a golden CSV. Rule: nothing else may convert a tick to a time.
findings.acceptance_test: 13-test suite passes against the real anchors (anchors exact, strictly monotone over 675 ticks, exact inverse, rollover, formats, +1 hour, deep-link params, rejects non-monotone, append-only extension); golden tick-clock.csv committed; validator V9 finds no other tick-to-time conversion.
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Historical/data consistency C- to B+ (with 03-05); Usability/learnability; H9 and H11 enabled
findings.correction: Decision (a) is sound; the reason given for rejecting (b) is overstated. 'Infeasible without inventing data' is not true, since the renderer already holds/forward-fills and re-timing would resample rather than invent. The decisive reasons are: 63 h at 5 min is about 757 ticks (>675, so tab ranges, tickMax and every key change), tick permanence for links/bookmarks/Watch Together, and the 1.5 min/tick resolution the charge needs. Module: 13/13 tests reproduce; add a guard so tickAfterMinutes cannot round to the same tick (no-op button).

findings.title: Adopt and review the time-facts anchor proposal, then refit with kinematic constraints
findings.evidence: time-facts-anchors.csv (33 anchors, statuses S/M/R/D) loads into the module unchanged (strictly increasing, 1..675, slopes 0.83-42.3 min/tick); module inverse matches the specialist's tick_under_proposed_anchors on 129/129 facts (worst 0.05 tick). Against sourced times today's label is off by mean 4.95 h and the map clock 4.98 h (n=134). Under the proposal 19 keyframe pairs still exceed speed caps (Hood/Law regiments 256-260 ~2 km in ~11 min; 302-308 cluster packed into 0.83 min/tick; charge pairs 544-551; XI Corps 65-68; 20th Maine 264-265; U-8NY-CAV 3-4). Anchors t75, t90, t248, t275, t538 are status R (need historian decision).
findings.root_cause: Authored labels and clocks were never tied to sourced times; some sim events sit on the wrong side of neighbours so no smooth warp satisfies both history and placements.
findings.fix: Import per mapping (tick, ISO time, status->conf A/B/C/D and sigma 10/15/30/30); historian review of R anchors; run fit-anchors: LNDS inversion triage, detrended isotonic regression (PAVA) with kinematic lower bounds L(t) (caps inf 150 / art 250 / cav 400 m/min), Douglas-Peucker eps=8 min keeping conf-A anchors and ticks 1/226/451/675, residual report, regenerate ticks.json and golden CSV. Slope policy: warn >15 (lull), error >60, min 0.75.
findings.acceptance_test: Every conf-A/B fact within 2 sigma of its fitted time; all slopes within [0.75, 60]; V6/V7 findings triaged; historian sign-off recorded; golden CSV diff reviewed.
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: C4 closed; content credibility
findings.correction: Numbers reproduce (33 anchors, slopes 0.83-42.33, 129/129 inverse, 4.95/4.98 h, the same 19 pairs). Anchor t5 (5:20 AM, status M) is circular: its evidence is 'site t5 label 5:20am ... keeps the pre-7:30 slope realistic' and it reuses fact R003 already used by t1. Mapping M to conf B/sigma 15 overstates it; import as derived (D, sigma 30) or drop it. Also record which authored claim loses where an anchor contradicts a data description (placements_day1_ticks101_225.json says ticks 101-225 span '1:30pm to 12:40am'; anchor t100 = 8:00 PM).

findings.title: Event registry (events.json); resolve cross-source tick disagreements and order inversions
findings.evidence: Same event on different ticks: first shot 12 vs scrubber marker 17; Ewell's order 75 (chronology) vs 175 (turning-points.html:58); Hancock wounded 550/554/552-570; Cushing 548/549/552/553; Hood 258/262/278; Vincent 270 vs 290; Weed/Hazlett 272 vs 293/295; 1st Minnesota 302 vs 295; 26th NC 16 vs 28; Iron Brigade 20 vs 27. Stop 8 (tick 270, 6:00 PM) precedes stop 7 (tick 275, 5:00 PM); stops 12/13/14 all '3:00 PM'. time-facts classifies 12 MISORDERED, 4 WRONG-DAY (ticks 8, 360, 380, 420), 9 COMPOSITE, 2 UNVERIFIED-QUOTE (525, 530) chronology events.
findings.root_cause: Ticks are retyped in 15+ structures (chronology, vignettes, successions, monuments, stops, turning points, quick picks, IF names, TO markers, Gc, sandbox); no single registry.
findings.fix: Create /data/events.json (id, aliases, tick, tick_end, real{best,start,end,sigma,fact}, anchor flag); every other file references event ids; re-tick or split events per time-facts section 7.4 suggestions (e.g. 360 to ~451, 380 to ~516, 420 to ~500, 460 to ~511) after map spot-check; split the 9 composites; verify or drop the two quotes.
findings.acceptance_test: Validator V5 (same event within +-2 ticks across files) and V6 (registry order non-decreasing within +-1 tick) clean.
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Historical/data consistency (C- to B+), credibility of every caption
findings.correction: Evidence confirmed (10 disagreement groups incl. 12/17, 75/175, 258/262/278, 270/290, 272/293/295, 548/549/552/553; succession ticks verified). Effort L is optimistic: 27 content defects (12 MISORDERED, 4 WRONG-DAY, 9 COMPOSITE, 2 UNVERIFIED-QUOTE) each need sourced re-ticking, map spot-check, new copy for the 9 splits, plus the Pickett placement audit: L-XL.

findings.title: Regenerate data-level time strings and metadata from the model
findings.evidence: chronology_day*.json time labels drift through 21 pace segments (+5, +15, then 0..-230 min); metadata.tick_formula ('Each tick = 5 minutes') false; placement_schema.json ticks_per_day real_time mixes 05:00 and 06:00 conventions and claims 430,000+ records / 600-700 units per tick (actual 1,804 / ~10); placements_day1_ticks1_50 record_count 4,890 vs 100 actual; chunk descriptions imply 5.1,5.3,5.4,5.0,2.8,4.3,3.8,4.4,3.9 min/tick; prose times contradict labels on the same record (t12 6:00am vs 'approximately 7:30am'; t518 9:30am vs 'approximately 1:00pm').
findings.root_cause: Labels were hand-authored per chunk; metadata describes intent, not data.
findings.fix: scripts/build-time-artifacts.mjs regenerates chronology time/time_display, tick_formula pointer, placement_schema real_time, chunk descriptions and record_count from the anchors; add structured duration_min to casualty engagement periods; keep legacy time field (regenerated) for >= 30 days so old bundles render.
findings.acceptance_test: Validator V3/V4/V13 clean; old bundle still renders event cards without 'undefined'.
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Historical/data consistency; Documentation accuracy
findings.correction: Drift table (21 segments, +5/+15/0..-230/-20..-215), chunk-description pace (within rounding), record_count 4,890 vs 100, schema '430000' and '600-700' all verified. Only the first placements file carries record_count.

findings.title: Deep-link consumer (urlState.js) with full backward compatibility
findings.evidence: bundle.pretty.js:101019 is the only URLSearchParams read (ancestor). Emitters: $k 97822-97830 (?t=&u=&z=&ll=); documentary.html:92, education.html:81, search.html:127, historian.html:110, embed.html:60 (?tick=&vignette=); turning-points.html:118; regiment.html:247 (?unit=&tick=); search.html:114 (?unit=) and :139 (?lat=&lng=). Guide promises 'Share a permalink'. Also true of the Jun-13 build.
findings.root_cause: Share/link builders were written without a reader; three key spellings for the same thing.
findings.fix: One parser/builder: accept tick, t, at (ISO local, only if no tick), av, unit/u, vignette (sets tick if absent), z, ll or lat+lng, ancestor, day; validate and clamp (tick regex ^\d{1,6}$, bounds from maxBounds 97244); skip the 3.5 s fast-forward splash and onboarding chooser when a deep link is present; history.replaceState to canonical form; emitters switch to canonical names while every alias keeps working.
findings.acceptance_test: Fixtures (?tick=538&vignette=V-016, /?unit=U-20ME&tick=267, ?t=28&u=U-I&z=15.0&ll=..., ?ancestor=..., ?at=1863-07-03T15:00, hostile junk) parse to safe values; e2e opens all 9 link builders' URLs at the right state with splash skipped.
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Core function (every 'See it on the map' link works), Usability; referral funnel
findings.correction: Emitters and the single reader (101019) verified; no ?tick= reader anywhere in index.html/site-nav.js. Corrections: (1) the lone reader is inside Zk, mounted only after Yn is toggled (initial false, 112952; mount 113251), so ?ancestor= never worked on cold load either, though the bundle emits it (101117) and the guide promises it (ug.txt:124); section 8's 'ancestor: existing, unchanged' is wrong, the parser must open the panel. (2) The consumer needs ensureDay: boot loads only Day 1 (sF 96940), Day 2/3 load only during playback at ticks >=200/>=420 (96991-96992) or on mobile at map load (103040-103042), and jumpToDay (9369) loads nothing, so ?tick=538 on desktop paints forward-filled Day-1 positions. (3) The splash resets currentTick to 1 on completion (101500), so it must be skipped, not raced.

findings.title: Seek-safe, gap-tolerant renderer state (stateAt) replacing the forward-fill cache
findings.evidence: const i2 = {} at 96265 written at 96271, never cleared, so a backward seek 500 to 20 draws units lacking an exact record at their tick-500 positions; y1 (96266-96310) and F4 (96238-96262) interpolate only between adjacent ticks, but only 93 of 1,209 consecutive-keyframe pairs are 1 tick apart (units hold then jump); minimap count uses records at exactly one tick (99821).
findings.root_cause: Global mutable cache and adjacent-tick-only interpolation over sparse keyframes.
findings.fix: Pure stateAt(tracks, tickFloat): per-unit binary search of keyframes, tick-space interpolation with existing disposition easing, MAX_GLIDE_TICKS and per-keyframe snap:true (day-boundary pairs 225-226 and 450-451 must be snap); minimap shows units on the field plus the clock.
findings.acceptance_test: e2e: play to 500, seek to 20, no unit rendered at a position from a keyframe with tick > 20; keyframe glide visible; minimap shows on-field count.
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Core function and Reliability (no stale positions), Fit & finish
findings.correction: Evidence exact (96238, 96265/96271, 96266-96310, 99821). Corrections: (1) the routine trigger is the boot splash (101494 sweeps the store 1 to 675; effects at 97312-97325 call y1 per tick change), priming i2 on every load. Simulation on the Day-1 files (the only ones loaded then): 186 units drawn at tick 1 vs 70 with a tick-1 row at 60 fps (120 at 30 fps, 97 at 20 fps); app-bugs.md says 261. Add acceptance test 'after boot, tick 1 shows only units with keyframe <=1'. (2) 'Build tracks once after load' fails under lazy per-day loading (addPlacementsForDay 9397-9406). (3) Section 7.1 says 'identical visuals' but the fix makes motion continuous, changing most of the 1,116 non-adjacent pairs; flag it and design MAX_GLIDE_TICKS per disposition. (4) Unify the OOB (50-tick, 102325) and roster (100-tick, 102664/103124) on-field windows.

findings.title: Crossing-based triggers with minute look-back; show the clock in cards, toasts and panels
findings.evidence: LF matches f.byTick[c] exactly (98607); vignette panel matches c, c-1, c-2 (98268-98272); Math.floor(Hc/Pe) can advance several ticks (96984); toast footer 'Tick N' (99949-99951), unit panel 'At Tick' (98031), succession '(tick N)' (97566), vignette jump button (98340-98343), ancestor rows QF (101078). Toasts (bF, 97569) already use the correct (prev, cur] rule. Chronology has 0 events for ticks 101-225.
findings.root_cause: Equality triggers and tick-labelled UI written for a uniform 5-min clock.
findings.fix: Fire when prevTick < event.tick <= curTick with a look-back of max(15 battle-min, 2 ticks); on seek show the latest event inside the look-back; replace every 'Tick N' label with tm.format(tick,'time') (tick moves to a tooltip); batch/cap toasts at 8x/16x.
findings.acceptance_test: At 16x with throttled frames every HIGH/CRITICAL card appears at least once; all panels show clock strings equal to the module's.
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Usability (no missed events), Reliability, H4 clutter
findings.correction: Exact-tick triggers (98607, 98268-98272, 96984) verified. 'Toasts already use the correct rule' is half true: qF updates H.current only while playing (99897-99903, guard precedes H.current = c), so after a paused seek (50 to 500) the first tick after Play evaluates bF(50,500) and queues up to 4 stale succession toasts. Inferred from code, not run.

findings.title: Playback semantics and labels: honest speed label, hour steps, tour windows, gaps, optional clock pacing
findings.evidence: cF=500 ms/tick (96948, 96982) = 2 ticks/s, i.e. 1.7 to 85 battle-min/s under the proposed anchors; label '1x (real time)' at 97429; +-12 ticks as 'one hour' at 112218-112219, 112310, 112334, 112979, 112984 and Help chunk; speed buttons cap 8x (112185) vs '+' key 16x (112998); tour tickWindow*500/2 (100337); gaps 226-240 (32 min/tick) and 515-518 (42 min/tick).
findings.root_cause: Playback and UI copy assume 1 tick = 5 min.
findings.fix: HUD '1x' plus live '~N min of battle per second'; Shift+arrows and buttons via tm.tickAfterMinutes(c, +-60); tour windows in battle minutes; honour anchors gaps[] (auto-accelerate + quiet-hours caption); optional 'clock' pacing mode (clockMin += dt*rate; tickFloat = minutesToTick) using the existing fractional ut at 97013; one shared speed cap.
findings.acceptance_test: Displayed rate equals measured battle-min/s within 5%; +1h moves 60 battle-min +- half a tick; at '60 min/s' one second advances the clock 1 hour +-1%.
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Usability/learnability (H9 closed), Accessibility (labelled controls)
findings.correction: 96948/96982 (2 ticks/s), 97429, the +/-12 sites (112218/112310/112334), 8x cap (112185) vs 16x, tour tickWindow*500/2 (100337) verified; 1.7-85 battle-min/s follows from slopes 0.83-42.3.

findings.title: Solar-driven day/night lighting (with moon cap) for the map, Camera and Immersive
findings.evidence: E4 thresholds (9861-9884) run ~1 h before computed sunset 19:32 (civil dusk ~20:05) and are fed the 05:00-base hour, so the Louisiana Tigers assault (V-014, tick 326, 'in near-darkness') renders at M4 hour 13.3 with zero tint while the toolbar reads 12:20 PM; Day-1 night ticks 100-225 render daylight until ~tick 145; camera.html:175-187 and immersive.html:163-173 use integer-hour tables; CSS transition 8s (9894) is wall-clock.
findings.root_cause: Lighting keyed to the wrong clock with hand-tuned thresholds.
findings.fix: sunState(tick) from the per-date solar table (sunrise ~04:35, sunset ~19:32, civil dawn/dusk ~04:02/20:05 local mean time; moon near full so cap night alpha ~0.35); drive overlay per frame from sunState (no CSS transition) in all three surfaces.
findings.acceptance_test: Visual snapshots at ticks 100 (dusk), 150 (night), 326 (dusk), 451 (first light), 538 (day) match expectations.
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Visual fidelity; Historical consistency
findings.correction: Tick 326 gives M4 hour 13.33, E4 alpha 0, toolbar 12:20 PM; V-014 contains 'near-darkness'; sunrise 04:35 / sunset 19:31 / civil 04:03-20:04 reproduced independently. Nit: E4's dusk ramp starts at hour 16 (band f<18), not 17, and dawn lags the other way (alpha 0.25 at 05:00-06:00 vs civil dawn 04:03); the solar function fixes both.

findings.title: Sub-pages adopt one shared time-model script
findings.evidence: Copy/pasted formulas: compare.html:114-129 (dead 'am (next day)' branch), living-ledger.html:64,90,135-144, camera.html:175-187, immersive.html:163-173, dashboard.html:85,141,163-166, documentary.html:84,89, education.html:63,72-73, regiment.html:189,218-219, cinematic-export.html:60-64,174-175,213-214,225-226,246, watch-together.html:172,192,201-202, search.html:125, historian.html:109; three different dayForTick copies; two date conventions.
findings.root_cause: No shared module for static pages.
findings.fix: One /js/time-model.js loaded as type=module (not via render-blocking site-nav.js) plus fetch of /data/time_anchors.json; delete per-page formulas; show clock as primary, tick as tooltip; canonical ?tick= links.
findings.acceptance_test: Same clock string at tick 538 on compare, living-ledger, camera, immersive, documentary, education, turning-points and sandbox (e2e 6).
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Fit & finish; consistency across 20 pages
findings.correction: Formulas at compare 120-129, ledger 135-144, camera 175-179, immersive 169-173 verified. Add to effort: the pages' inline scripts are classic IIFEs (compare.html:95, living-ledger.html:87, camera.html:62), so adopting an ES module needs type=module conversion or dynamic import().

findings.title: Generate captions from the model; fix known wrong labels
findings.evidence: sandbox.html:103-107 presets wrong vs site's own chronology (tick 260 'before Longstreet's assault' but t256 is the assault; tick 553 'before the charge reaches the wall' but t551 Armistead over the wall and t553 Cushing KIA; tick 62 'mid-morning, I Corps holding' but t62 is 'I Corps right flank crumbling' and stop 3 says 2:30 PM); turning-points.html:58 tick 175; compare.html:55 hint = ticks 358/382 under its own formula; mon_hood tooltip '8:00 AM July 4' above '4:00 PM July 2'; onboarding tick 267 'July 2 afternoon' beside a 7:25 AM clock.
findings.root_cause: Typed times and day-part words beside ticks with no validation.
findings.fix: th, mA, zF, IF, TO, Gc, sandbox, compare, turning-points reference registry ids and render '{title} - {format}' (day-part computed from the model + solar table); remove typed clock strings.
findings.acceptance_test: Validator V3 clean on these files; the three sandbox labels and turning point 175 corrected.
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Historical/data consistency; copy voice
findings.correction: Sandbox presets 103-107, chronology t62/t256/t260/t551/t553 texts, turning-points tick 175 vs chronology 75, compare hint line 55 all verified.

findings.title: Rollout hygiene: content-hashed names, service worker and data cache policy, anchors versioning
findings.evidence: assets/index-Cg8FAMXN.js is 2,280,438 bytes in the Sep-29 deploy vs 2,280,095 in the Jul-20 folder under the same name (differs from byte 151,648) while /assets/* is `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and sw.js (41-50) is cache-first with PRECACHE_ASSETS naming it (sw.js:5-6, CACHE_NAME 'gbg-v5' at line 3); prov-recon T-02 counts four byte-streams under one name; /data/* max-age=3600; first-visit controllerchange reload (index.html:258-270).
findings.root_cause: In-place patching of a hash-named file; no cache-busting discipline.
findings.fix: Every patch gets a new content-hash filename with index.html, sw.js (PRECACHE_ASSETS + CACHE_NAME bump) updated together; assert sha256(file)[:8]===name in CI; serve time_anchors/events/ticks JSON with max-age=0,must-revalidate; put anchors version (av) in bookmarks and watch-together messages; keep regenerated legacy chronology time for >= 30 days; fix C6 first or together.
findings.acceptance_test: A browser holding the Sep-29 bundle receives the new bundle on next load; CI hash assertion passes.
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Reliability, Performance (stale-bundle cache), release hygiene
findings.correction: Bytes (2,280,438 live vs 2,280,095 Jul-20, first diff at byte 151,648), immutable and no-store headers, sw.js lines, and prov-recon T-02 corroboration verified. Corrections: (1) rename cascade to the two lazy chunks (see 01). open_questions: Historical truth of the anchors belongs to the time-facts specialist, whose CSVs were still changing while I worked. The anchor list went from 35 to 33 rows as the 225/450 boundary rows were dropped. I checked the proposal for internal consistency only, not against 1863 sources.
Five anchors are status R and need a historian's decision (t75, t90, t248, t275, t538), and the time of Colgrove's charge is contested.

Product decisions: Day tabs anchored to first light (recommended) vs midnight; whether to show 'about'/'c.' prefixes; whether the 'clock' playback mode is exposed in the UI; whether the 125 event-less Day-1 night ticks (18.5% of the timeline) keep their ~4 min/tick density or become a flagged time-lapse; whether to append an optional July-4 stub at ticks 676+.
The intent of the 06:00/04:00 store constants is undocumented. I found no README, PENDING or comment mentioning them.
Sunrise/sunset/twilight/moon values come from the time-facts specialist's NOAA script, which I re-ran. Moon phase is a mean-synodic estimate (+-0.5 d). Neither was cross-checked against an almanac.

The claim that desktop overlays render in the Mobile layout comes from static reading of the render tree (113242-113283). It was not measured, and the identification with the 572 px transport row is an inference.
No browser was used, so all behaviour is derived from source, data and scripts. Runtime feel, such as how 24-32 min per tick reads at 1x, should be judged in the Phase-2 A/B overlay.
The NPS Auto Tour source PDFs (Gettysburg_Auto_Tour_Stops*.pdf in Downloads) were not read. The tour-stop clock times may derive from them.

The kinematic checks use straight-line distances, so they are lower bounds on required time. The 19 pairs flagged under the current anchors need triage to separate data defects from anchors that should sit further apart.
verification_summary:
The app-time report is largely accurate. Every bundle.pretty.js line number I checked was exact, and the numbers I re-derived reproduced: 1,804 records, 6 and 19 speed-cap pairs, 33 anchors, the 4.95 h mean error, 21 drift segments, and 13/13 tests plus 129/129 inverse checks. Jun-13/Jul-20 regression archaeology, live headers and byte sizes also match. No finding was refuted. Nine were confirmed outright. Eleven need corrections, mostly where the proposed fix would not work as written, and I found 8 missed issues. All of this is appended to app-time.md under "## Verification".

The main corrections:
- **Rename cascade (01, 13).** HelpModal and BookmarkPanel are immutable chunks that import "./index-Cg8FAMXN.js", so renaming the entry bundle must also rewrite and rename them. Otherwise opening Help or Bookmarks loads a second copy of the old entry, with duplicate React and store.
- **CI hash check (13).** The proposed sha256(file)[:8] === name assertion can never pass. None of the five shipped assets matches its name in hex or base64url, because Rollup hashes pre-render, not the final bytes.
- **Deploy gate (14).** The plan gates on a Netlify `[build] command`, but the site is deployed by drag-and-drop, which runs no build. The check needs to be a local pre-deploy step.
- **Mobile overlays (20).** The report calls the overlay-mounting bug an inference and rates it medium. It is confirmed: the desktop time bar ties on z-index with the mobile root, and DOM order puts it on top. Severity should be high, and it is a one-change fix for audit criticals C1 and C2 that belongs in Phase 0. Unmount selectively: the mobile layout has no counterpart for the event card, story panel or toasts.
- **Deep links (06).** The only URL reader sits inside the ancestor panel, which mounts only when the user opens it, so the ancestor deep link has never worked on a cold load. A deep-link consumer also needs each day's data loaded first, because Day 2/3 placements only load during playback.
- **Seek and splash bug (07).** The stale forward-fill cache is primed by the boot splash on every page load, not only by backward seeks. In my simulation, tick 1 draws 186 units instead of 70 at 60 fps.
- **Phase 0 claim (01).** The report says Phase 0 removes the contradictory monument tooltips. It does not; only the date is repaired.
- **Toasts (08).** The "toasts already use the correct rule" claim is only half true. After a paused seek, the first tick of playback replays up to four stale toasts.
- **Internal inconsistencies (17).** The report says "5 of the 19 pairs are day seams" in one place and 1 in another; 1 is correct. It also says the Day-1 night keeps "~2.6 min/tick" where the proposed anchors give 4.05.

missed_by_specialist.title: Toast burst after a paused seek (stale prev tick)
missed_by_specialist.evidence: qF (bundle.pretty.js:99888-99960): effect returns at `if (!P || !f) return;` before `H.current = c` (99897-99900), so H.current is not updated while paused. Seek 50 to 500, press Play: bF(50,500) (97569 filter approx_tick > c && <= f) returns every succession in range and slice(-4) shows 4 arbitrary old toasts. Report app-time-08 says toasts already use the correct rule.
missed_by_specialist.fix: Update H.current on every tick change (before the isPlaying guard) or reset it on seek; cap/batch toasts. Add a test: seek while paused then Play produces zero toasts.

missed_by_specialist.title: Boot splash primes the never-cleared forward-fill cache on every page load
missed_by_specialist.evidence: tO sets currentTick 1..675 through the store (bundle.pretty.js:101494); effects at 97312-97325 call y1(...,0) on each change, writing i2 (96271). Simulation with the Day-1 data files (only Day 1 loaded then): 186 units drawn at tick 1 vs 70 with a tick-1 row at 60 fps (120 at 30 fps, 97 at 20 fps); app-bugs.md estimates 261. app-time-07 attributes the defect only to backward seeks and its acceptance test is seek 500 to 20.
missed_by_specialist.fix: stateAt (as proposed) plus an acceptance test 'after boot, tick 1 renders exactly the units with a keyframe <= 1'. Short-term: clear i2 whenever tick moves backward or by more than 1, and stop the splash writing to the real store.

missed_by_specialist.title: Tick-count look-back windows are minute-blind
missed_by_specialist.evidence: Succession highlight `Math.abs(x - z.successionTick) < 10` (97584); OOB panel looks back 50 ticks (102325); roster 100 ticks (102664) and mobile roster 100 (103124); event-card dismiss reset `Math.abs(c - P) > 1` (98602). At 0.83-42.3 min/tick these windows span 40 min to about 35 h. Report section 7.2 converts only tour windows.
missed_by_specialist.fix: Express each window in battle minutes and convert with tm.tickAfterMinutes / minutesToTick; unify OOB/roster/map on-field definitions.

missed_by_specialist.title: Deep links and day tabs need ensureDay: Day 2/3 placement data loads only during playback
missed_by_specialist.evidence: Boot loads zp(1) only (bundle.pretty.js:96940); zp(2)/zp(3) fire only inside the playing branch of Ed at ticks >=200 / >=420 (96991-96992) or on mobile map load (103040-103042); jumpToDay (9369-9370) just sets currentTick. So desktop ?tick=538, the 2/3 keys and day tabs show forward-filled Day-1 positions until Play. app-time-06 does not require loading data before applying a deep-linked tick.
missed_by_specialist.fix: Add `await ensureDay(1..day(tick))` (retry, in-flight dedupe; see app-bugs.md app-bugs-05) to the deep-link consumer and jumpToDay; rebuild stateAt tracks per loaded day.
